value_sources.note: Not part of A SET: Fanatec's 2022 GT7 page sets Countersteering Assist Off for wheel users.

FFS.note: Not offered with the Boost Kit on base firmware 1.9.0.2 or later (Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 changelog), but Fanatec help articles updated in September 2026 still describe LIN/PEAK. If your Advanced menu still shows FFS, set PEA (LIN caps the base at about 6 Nm).

BRAKE_LINEARITY.note: Leave Brake Linearity at the wheel preset's default and let the rig check decide: sources split 0 / 3 / 25, EA's gamepad default is 25 and the PS5 wheel default is unverified.

derivations.SETUP: pitwall's slot suggestion (rig-setup-sources.md 6.0): 1 SET F1 25, 2 SET GT7 custom, 3 SET experiments. Any custom slot works; custom slots save each change immediately.
derivations.PIT_STOP_EFFECTS: Not listed by the source; pitwall sets 0 because it has no driving effect.
derivations.COUNTERSTEERING_ASSIST: Fanatec's GT7 advice for wheel users (Off), applied by pitwall to this style.
derivations.VIB_FFB: Force feedback must be on for any FFB setting to apply.
derivations.BRAKE_DEADZONE: F1 25 calibration baseline (rig-setup-sources.md 6.0): 0, or 1-3 only if the rig check finds brake input at rest.
derivations.BRAKE_SATURATION: F1 25 calibration baseline (rig-setup-sources.md 6.0): 0. Fix the pedal range in hardware (press-fully routine, BRF), not with saturation.
derivations.THROTTLE_DEADZONE: F1 25 calibration baseline (rig-setup-sources.md 6.0): 0 unless the rig check finds throttle input at rest.
derivations.THROTTLE_SATURATION: F1 25 calibration baseline (rig-setup-sources.md 6.0): 0 unless the rig check finds 100% throttle is not reached.

skill_strength_scale.explanation: pitwall rule, no published source: a beginner or young driver gets a lighter wheel by scaling base FF in their own custom slot. Lower peak torque means a gentler wheel when the car spins or hits a kerb, and less fatigue. Base FF caps every force the base sends; the endstop does not depend on FF on current firmware. The default was set on the 5 Nm base: on a stronger base it shrinks by the ratio of the two tables' peak torques (60% becomes 40% at 8 Nm), so the Boost Kit does not make the wheel heavier. A force the driver sets on the slider is used as given.

beginner_ndp_floor.explanation: pitwall rule: NDP is Fanatec's first fix for oscillation and wheel speed in oversteer, so a beginner gets at least NDP 20 (Fanatec's 2026 F1 value) instead of OFF.

driver_slot.explanation: pitwall rule: a driver with a lighter wheel gets their own spare custom slot (4 SET or 5 SET), so switching drivers is one menu change.

SEN.note: Strong around 360 (Fanatec: matches a real F1 wheel). Esports 300-360, SimRacingSetup 380, Matt212 400.

FFS.note: Unanimous where present. Not offered with the Boost Kit on FullForce firmware.

VIB_FFB_STRENGTH.note: Split by game version and style, not by torque: no credible source lowers it from 5 to 8 Nm (rig-setup-sources.md 5.2). Carson at 8 Nm went 55-70 (F1 24), 75-90 (F1 25), 90-100 (after v1.25).

RUMBLE_STRIP_EFFECTS.note: Same split; Fanatec 2026 lowered it to 0-20.

WHEEL_DAMPER.note: Fanatec's Xbox column uses 5; a generic-wheel guide's 10 is an outlier.

BRAKE_LINEARITY.note: Carson 0, F1withNick 3, Opmeer and THOMB 25 (the default per Opmeer). No CSL LC owner data.

BRF.note: CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit owners, stock elastomers, latest value per owner (GTPlanet 2022-2023, mostly GT7 on PS5). Other pedal models do not transfer; revision 1's mixed median of 48 is withdrawn.

SEN.note: One user ran 600 for GT3 cars.

FF.note: The post-hotfix comfort setup tuned down to 70.

NDP.note: Fanatec 38; A SET readout 40; post-hotfix custom 16.

INT.note: Abarth_71's 15 is the outlier; A SET readout 4.

SPR.note: Fanatec known issue: SPR/DPR do not work in GT7 menus on the GT DD Pro; users say they do nothing while driving.

FUL.note: Default 100 after the hotfix; interim advice was below 100 or OFF.

FFB_MAX_TORQUE.note: Pre-1.71 5-6 (3-7 by class). Post-1.71 guidance 4-5 with A SET; 8 Nm reports run 5-10 with no consensus.

FFB_SENSITIVITY.note: 1 (most) versus 10 (Matika, Abarth_71). Before the hotfix high Sensitivity with high torque and FUL was linked to disconnects.

BRF.note: CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit owners, stock elastomers, latest value per owner (GTPlanet 2022-2023, mostly GT7 on PS5). No owner report after 1.71.

known_issues.title: F1 25 v1.25: the wheel oscillates or loses FFB after a session change
known_issues.detail: Since v1.25 (2026-09-07) CSL DD / GT DD Pro owners report violent left-right oscillation or lost FFB after a session change or restart (for example Qualifying to Race), until the base is power-cycled. Pause and power-cycle the base; do not tune NDP, INT or the damper against it (it happened at NDP 50 / INT 11, and FUL OFF did not help). Every report that states a torque is at 8 Nm, and no PS5 report was found. EA confirmed it and shared a fix with Fanatec on 2026-10-07 (no ETA). The rig check flags it as 'Oscillation after a session change'.
known_issues.source: EA forums threads 13695137, 13701405, 13701710; forum.fanatec.com topic 20597 (PS5 impact unverified)

known_issues.title: F1 25 v1.25: FFB reported lighter
known_issues.detail: Players on several brands report lighter or less detailed FFB after v1.25, so values from before September may feel lighter. Carson raised his 8 Nm strength by 10-20. Start at the upper end of a published range and adjust by feel.

known_issues.title: FFS (Peak/Linear) is gone with the Boost Kit on current firmware
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 (base 1.9.0.2) removed FFS for Boost Kit bases and raised holding torque from 6 to 8 Nm. Fanatec help articles updated in September 2026 still describe LIN/PEAK, so check the Advanced menu once the kit is fitted; set PEA only if FFS is still shown.

known_issues.title: Slots may report different maximum torque
known_issues.detail: One user saw the PC App report 8 Nm in AUTO and slot 5 but 6 Nm in slots 1-4. Check what your slots report after fitting the Boost Kit.

known_issues.title: GT DD Pro can lose FFB in GT7 (wheel may spin)
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue. Not a tuning mistake. If it happens: FUL 60, then OFF; then FF 80-90 and a lower Sensitivity.

known_issues.title: SPR and DPR do not work in GT7 menus on the GT DD Pro
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue; users say they do nothing while driving.

known_issues.title: GT7 Spec IV Part 1 is reported for 2026-10-15
known_issues.detail: Headline only. Re-check GT7 values and rerun the rig check after it.

known_issues.title: FullForce weaker than intended on CSL DD / GT DD Pro
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue. No source shows that F1 25 implements FullForce: leave FUL at its default for F1.

known_issues.title: SEN AUTO misbehaves in F1 games
known_issues.detail: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 known issue (seen on PC). Set SEN by hand to the in-game rotation.

known_issues.title: The Fanatec mobile app does not work with the new Windows App
known_issues.detail: Its own release notes say so. There is no console path for base settings on PS5 other than the on-wheel Tuning Menu.
known_issues.source: Fanatec App 1.6.1.3 release notes; App Store listing

known_issues.title: F1 25: a small FFB bump when Straight Mode switches
known_issues.detail: Reported by a DD+ owner on PS5 Pro. Not a fault; the rig check ignores it.

known_issues.title: F1 25: FFB dropping mid-race on PS5
known_issues.detail: Community reports; toggling Vibration & Force Feedback restored it.

boost_kit.text: Fit the Boost Kit 180 in place of the standard PSU. The base detects it and releases 8 Nm automatically; there is no setup step.
boost_kit.source: Fanatec help 30312080999825; GT DD Pro manual 5.6.4

boost_kit.text: Check FFS on your base: it is not offered with the Boost Kit on base firmware 1.9.0.2 or later. If it is still shown, set PEA (LIN caps the base at about 6 Nm). Note what each slot reports as maximum torque.
boost_kit.source: Fanatec App 1.5.1.2 release notes; slot report GTPlanet 2026-09-12 (unverified)

boost_kit.text: The endstop does not depend on FF on current firmware, so a lower FF never weakens it.
Holding torque is now 8 Nm (firmware 1.9.0.2 or later), so long high-load corners feel heavier than on older-firmware 8 Nm presets.
Expect more hands-off oscillation at 8 Nm. With NDP OFF you may need NDP 5-20: raise it in steps of 5 and compare the rig check before and after.
boost_kit.source: viewer comments on Fin's 8 Nm video; Fanatec oscillation guide

boost_kit.text: F1 25 v1.25: if the wheel oscillates or loses FFB after a session change, pause and power-cycle the base. Every report that states a torque is at 8 Nm. Do not tune against it.
Keep airflow around the base (it is passively cooled). Fanatec publishes no thermal data for the GT DD Pro at 8 Nm.

csl.text: After every power-on, press the throttle and brake fully once and release them before driving.
csl.detail: The CSL Pedals calibrate min/max automatically as they are pressed; until then the readings can be wrong.
csl.source: Fanatec CSL Pedals product page, Explorer guide and Pedals FAQ

csl.text: Nothing to set on the pedals: the stock brake measures travel with a 12-bit Hall sensor (not a potentiometer). There is no BRF and no manual calibration.
The pedals connect by RJ12 to the wheel base (the only path on a console).
GT7 has no documented in-game pedal calibration (one unverified claim of an Options > Controllers calibration: check on your PS5). The pedals work as calibrated.
After a session, open the rig check: brake input at rest, whether 100% throttle and brake are reached, how long the brake sits at 100% and whether the peaks drift during the session.

csl_load_cell.text: Update the base firmware before installing the kit (Windows PC, Fanatec App, base in RED mode). Then back to DARK BLUE, recalibrate the wheel centre and recheck your slots.
csl_load_cell.source: Fanatec Load Cell Kit manual; App 1.6.1.3 notes

csl_load_cell.text: Wiring: RJ12 from the accelerator's 'Wheel Base / Load Cell' port to the load cell's 'Load Cell' port, accelerator to the base. Never connect RJ12 and USB at the same time.
csl_load_cell.source: Fanatec CSL Pedals Load Cell Kit manual

csl_load_cell.text: Set BRF in the Tuning Menu (it appears in the Standard menu too once the load cell is detected). Start at the value in the wheel table.

Tune BRF so a firm press you can repeat every lap reaches 100%, not your maximum effort. Do 10 identical stops: if the peaks vary a lot, lower BRF; if 100% comes too easily (long plateaus at 100% in the rig check), raise it.
csl_load_cell.detail: Roughly 70-80% of your physical limit; reaching 100% should not need straining or lifting off the seat. A light stand or Playseat forces a lower BRF.
csl_load_cell.source: EveZone and SimXPro load-cell guides (community method)

csl_load_cell.text: After every power-on, press each pedal fully once (hold the brake at maximum for 2-3 s) and release. There is no manual calibration without a PC.
csl_load_cell.source: Fanatec Pedals FAQ; community note on the hold

csl_load_cell.text: Locking too easily? Raise BRF, lower Brake Pressure in the F1 25 car setup, or add brake linearity. BLI is not available (it needs ClubSport V3 pedals).
csl_load_cell.source: Fanatec Tuning Menu article; Trophi/Driver61 braking guides

csl_load_cell.text: GT7: BRF is the only lever. 2022 reports describe the load-cell brake as very sensitive in GT7 (a resting foot registers); 1.71 changed brake input, so recheck with the rig check.

These are hardware faults, not reasons to change BRF: the peak suddenly far below 100% at your usual press, the signal oscillating under constant pressure, a light press reading full brake, or input with your foot off the pedal. Recheck BRF on the wheel, update firmware, then contact support.
Manual min/max calibration needs a Windows PC and is reset by a load-cell firmware update. If the brake reads input at rest, Fanatec's fix is a firmware update plus a pedal reset via PC.
The old CSL brake can be refitted as a clutch; F1 25 and GT7 do not need one.
Run the rig check after fitting and compare it with a session from before the upgrade.

rig_check.label: Throttle at rest
rig_check.deviation: The research target is exactly 0; pitwall passes up to 0.5% because 12-bit pedals read a few thousandths at rest (0.002% on the real PS5 race).

rig_check.label: Full throttle reached
rig_check.threshold_note: The 90% limit is sourced for F1 25 since v1.25 (S Mode/DRS needs throttle above 90%); the 99% target is a pitwall heuristic.

rig_check.label: Time to peak brake
rig_check.reference: ACC GT3 0.31-0.38 s (Joyce et al. 2025); not F1

rig_check.label: Trail-brake release
rig_check.reference: ACC GT3 0.94-1.26 s (Joyce et al. 2025); not F1

rig_check.label: DRS closed by a light brake touch
Brake peak drift in the session
rig_check.threshold_note: Median peak of the last three firm stops minus the first three (single-press stops entered above 250 km/h, at least six). The research compares stops 8-10 with stops 1-3 at a similar entry speed; on real races that mixed light lifts with full stops and drift came out at +-30 points from driving alone, so pitwall compares firm stops only. The fail limit is a pitwall heuristic.

rig_check.label: Brake noise in steady holds
rig_check.threshold_note: The threshold is for the load cell; with the Hall brake the value is shown for comparison only.

rig_check.label: Steering oscillation on straights
rig_check.reference: Uncalibrated: hands-on driving already produces small corrections. Compare before and after a change (for example the Boost Kit).

rig_check.label: Oscillation after a session change
rig_check.threshold_note: Bursts of 3+ steering reversals larger than 10% of lock while standing still or with no pedal input, in the first 30 s of the session's first lap (pitwall heuristic; standing still is added to the research definition because drivers rev on the grid). Paused and garage frames are not recorded.

rig_check.label: Steering reversal rate
rig_check.reference: Driver-relative smoothness indicator (Markkula & Engstrom 2006). Compare with your own best sessions.
